I'm weighing the introduction's rating: its operator is vague and one citation is a Wikipedia page, so I'm leaning toward a 6 rather than a 7.

I'm checking the orbit section now: the 600 km sun-synchronous inclination of about 97.8° looks right, and a retrograde orbit fits an inclination above 90°. The reasoning about the launch vehicle and the Wikipedia citation are still open problems to flag.

I'm checking the orbit's RAAN of 27.33°, which I'd read as pointing to the launch site, but that's not how RAAN works, and Kourou sits at about −52.8° longitude. The ground track also seems to place the satellite over Australia, so the orbit and the launch location don't line up yet.

I'm checking the rest of the orbit section: the RAAN and ground track still don't line up with Kourou, and the element table has no epoch. The 600 km altitude is described as giving daily coverage with no swath calculations behind it, and the swath, resolution and altitude reasoning contradicts itself, so I need to flag that.

I'm checking the perturbation and manoeuvre claims from the executive summary, since no delta-v or perturbation calculation appears in the body. The ground station needs a check too: Mount Pleasant sits near -42°, which isn't polar, so the access-frequency justification is weak, and I still need to verify the two-telescope receiver claim.

I'm checking the access table next, and it has a problem: the last row repeats the one before it exactly, so there's a duplicate entry. The summary statistics still hold up if I count all 15 values, though, since the mean times 15 gives the stated total.

Now I'm checking the access-duration totals, adding up the listed values to see whether the stated total includes the duplicate row and the unlabelled first entry.

I'm checking the access statistics against the listed durations: the 15 values, including the stray "----" row, add up to the stated total and give the stated mean. I'm noting that the ground-station access windows are shown on the ground track figure, and that the text claims the satellite is always in sunlight on the descending pass. For a dawn-dusk sun-synchronous orbit at this altitude that claim doesn't hold, so I'm flagging it as a technical error.

I'm checking whether the sun-synchronous claim about daytime passes holds up: it depends on the local time of the descending node, which the text never states, so the claim is unsupported as written.

I'm checking the figure labelling now: the two orbit views, 12 hours apart, have no figure numbers or titles, only the caption under the second one. The inclination-versus-altitude plot likewise has no caption, and I'm moving on to the ground-track images.

I'm checking the image captions and the table layout next: the COE table has no number or caption, and the launch-manifest tables have garbled citations that point to references missing from the bibliography.

I also want to flag the statement that Vega E makes its first launch in 2024, since I can't verify it and it reads as outdated.

The orbit section's claim that it can launch directly into LEO contradicts that too, so I'll flag it.

I'm checking the launch-window reasoning next: the claim that there are two windows per day because the inclination exceeds the site latitude is muddled, and the text gives no launch azimuth or delta-v check to back it up.

I'm working through requirements R1 to R6 now. R1 and R3 are met, since the mission is clearly about monitoring coral reefs on the Great Barrier Reef with fluid lensing.
